The secondary mirror is convex, with focal length: \[f_2 = \frac{R_2}{2} = \frac{140\text{ mm}}{2} = +70\text{ mm}\] Using the mirror equation: \[\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f_2} \implies \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f_2} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{+70} - \frac{1}{+90} = \frac{9 - 7}{630} = \frac{2}{630} = \frac{1}{315}\text{ mm}^{-1}\] \[v = +315\text{ mm} = 31.5\text{ cm}\]

Step 4: Check and Interpretation
The positive value means the image is formed \(315\text{ mm}\) in front of the secondary mirror (towards the primary mirror, passing through the hole in the primary mirror to reach the eyepiece).

Step 5: Final Answer
The final image is formed at a distance of \(315\text{ mm}\) (or \(31.5\text{ cm}\)) from the secondary mirror.

Step 1: प्राथमिक दर्पण पर प्रथम परावर्तन
अनंत से आने वाली समानांतर किरणें अवतल प्राथमिक दर्पण के फोकस पर अभिसरित होती हैं: \[f_1 = \frac{R_1}{2} = \frac{220}{2} = 110\text{ mm}\]

Step 2: द्वितीयक दर्पण के लिए आभासी वस्तु
उत्तल द्वितीयक दर्पण प्राथमिक दर्पण से \(20\text{ mm}\) आगे स्थित है, अतः अभिसरण बिंदु की द्वितीयक दर्पण से दूरी: \[u = +(110 - 20) = +90\text{ mm}\] यह एक आभासी वस्तु का कार्य करता है।

Step 3: द्वितीयक दर्पण के लिए दर्पण सूत्र
उत्तल दर्पण की फोकस दूरी: \(f_2 = R_2/2 = +70\text{ mm}\)। \[\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{70} - \frac{1}{90} = \frac{2}{630} = \frac{1}{315}\text{ mm}^{-1} \implies v = +315\text{ mm} = 31.5\text{ cm}\]

Step 4: व्याख्या
प्रतिबिम्ब द्वितीयक दर्पण से \(315\text{ mm}\) की दूरी पर प्राथमिक दर्पण के छिद्र से गुजरते हुए बनता है।

Step 5: अंतिम उत्तर
अंतिम प्रतिबिम्ब द्वितीयक दर्पण से \(315\text{ mm}\) (या \(31.5\text{ cm}\)) की दूरी पर बनता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAY_OPTICS_MCQ_Q48 - Refractive index of liquid using lens and plane mirror

questiontext.text:
An equiconvex glass lens of refractive index \(1.50\) is placed on top of a liquid layer spread over a horizontal plane mirror. A small pin moved along the vertical axis coincides with its own inverted image at a distance of \(45.0\text{ cm}\) from the lens. When the liquid layer is completely removed and the experiment is repeated, the pin coincides with its inverted image at \(30.0\text{ cm}\). What is the refractive index of the liquid?

क्षैतिज समतल दर्पण पर फैली द्रव की परत के ऊपर \(1.50\) अपवर्तनांक का एक सम-उत्तल काँच का लेंस रखा गया है। ऊर्ध्वाधर अक्ष के अनुदिश गतिमान एक छोटी पिन लेंस से \(45.0\text{ cm}\) की दूरी पर अपने ही उल्टे प्रतिबिम्ब से संपाती होती है। जब द्रव की परत को पूरी तरह हटाकर प्रयोग दोहराया जाता है, तो पिन \(30.0\text{ cm}\) पर संपाती होती है। द्रव का अपवर्तनांक क्या है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Focal Length of Convex Lens Alone
When the needle coincides with its inverted image above the plane mirror, rays emerging from the lens must be parallel and strike the plane mirror normally, retracing their path. Thus, the measured distance is the focal length of the optical system.
Without the liquid, the focal length of the glass lens alone is \(f_1 = 30.0\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Radius of Curvature of the Equiconvex Lens
Using the lens maker's formula with \(n_g = 1.50\), \(R_1 = R\), \(R_2 = -R\): \[\frac{1}{f_1} = (n_g - 1)\frac{2}{R} = (1.50 - 1)\frac{2}{R} = \frac{1}{R} \implies R = f_1 = 30.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 3: Effective Focal Length with Liquid Layer
With the liquid layer present, the system consists of the equiconvex glass lens (focal length \(f_1 = +30.0\text{ cm}\)) in contact with a plano-concave liquid lens of focal length \(f_2\). The effective focal length is \(F = +45.0\text{ cm}\). \[\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2} \implies \frac{1}{f_2} = \frac{1}{F} - \frac{1}{f_1} = \frac{1}{45.0} - \frac{1}{30.0} = \frac{2 - 3}{90.0} = -\frac{1}{90.0}\text{ cm}^{-1}\] \[f_2 = -90.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 4: Refractive Index of the Liquid
The liquid lens is plano-concave with curved surface of radius \(R_1 = -R = -30.0\text{ cm}\) and flat surface \(R_2 = \infty\): \[\frac{1}{f_2} = (n_l - 1)\left(-\frac{1}{R}\right) \implies -\frac{1}{90.0} = (n_l - 1)\left(-\frac{1}{30.0}\right)\] \[n_l - 1 = \frac{30.0}{90.0} = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.3333\] \[n_l = 1 + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33\]

Step 5: Final Answer
The refractive index of the liquid is \(1.33\) (or \(4/3\)).

Step 1: केवल उत्तल लेंस की फोकस दूरी
द्रव के बिना, समतल दर्पण से परावर्तित होकर किरणें अपने मार्ग पर वापस लौटती हैं जब वस्तु फोकस पर होती है। अतः केवल काँच के लेंस की फोकस दूरी \(f_1 = 30.0\text{ cm}\) है।

Step 2: सम-उत्तल लेंस की वक्रता त्रिज्या
\[\frac{1}{f_1} = (1.50 - 1)\frac{2}{R} = \frac{1}{R} \implies R = 30.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 3: द्रव लेंस की फोकस दूरी
संयोजन की कुल फोकस दूरी \(F = 45.0\text{ cm}\) है: \[\frac{1}{f_2} = \frac{1}{45.0} - \frac{1}{30.0} = -\frac{1}{90.0}\text{ cm}^{-1} \implies f_2 = -90.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 4: द्रव का अपवर्तनांक
समतलोवतल द्रव लेंस के लिए \(R_1 = -30.0\text{ cm}\) तथा \(R_2 = \infty\): \[-\frac{1}{90.0} = (n_l - 1)\left(-\frac{1}{30.0}\right) \implies n_l - 1 = \frac{1}{3} \implies n_l = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33\]

Step 5: अंतिम उत्तर
द्रव का अपवर्तनांक \(1.33\) (या \(4/3\)) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q01 - Reflection laws and spherical mirror focal length

questiontext.text:
Statement I: The laws of reflection hold good at each point of any reflecting surface, whether plane or curved.

Statement II: For a spherical mirror of small aperture, the focal length is approximately equal to half of its radius of curvature.

कथन I: परावर्तन के नियम किसी भी परावर्तक सतह, चाहे वह समतल हो या वक्र, के प्रत्येक बिंदु पर मान्य होते हैं।

कथन II: छोटे द्वारक वाले गोलीय दर्पण के लिए, फोकस दूरी उसकी वक्रता त्रिज्या की लगभग आधी होती है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Reflection
The fundamental laws of reflection—namely, that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and that the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane—are strictly valid at every local point of incidence on any smooth reflecting boundary, regardless of whether the boundary is flat or curved.

Step 2: Evaluation of Spherical Mirror Focal Length
For spherical mirrors under the paraxial ray approximation (where ray angles with the principal axis and aperture size are small), geometric derivation gives \(f = \frac{R}{2}\), meaning the focal length is exactly half of the radius of curvature.

Step 3: Verification and Conclusion
Both stated principles are physically accurate and well-established in geometrical optics. Thus, both statements are correct.

चरण 1: परावर्तन का मूलभूत सिद्धांत
परावर्तन के मूलभूत नियम—अर्थात आपतन कोण परावर्तन कोण के बराबर होता है, तथा आपतित किरण, परावर्तित किरण और अभिलंब एक ही तल में होते हैं—किसी भी चिकनी परावर्तक सीमा के प्रत्येक स्थानीय आपतन बिंदु पर पूरी तरह मान्य होते हैं, चाहे सतह समतल हो या वक्र।

चरण 2: गोलीय दर्पण की फोकस दूरी का मूल्यांकन
उपाक्षीय किरणों (पैराक्सियल किरणों) के सन्निकटन के तहत, जहां किरणें मुख्य अक्ष के साथ बहुत छोटे कोण बनाती हैं और द्वारक छोटा होता है, ज्यामितीय व्युत्पत्ति से \(f = \frac{R}{2}\) प्राप्त होता है, जिसका अर्थ है कि फोकस दूरी वक्रता त्रिज्या की आधी होती है।

चरण 3: सत्यापन एवं निष्कर्ष
प्रस्तुत किए गए दोनों सिद्धांत भौतिक रूप से पूर्णतः सही हैं। अतः दोनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q02 - Characteristics of real and virtual optical images

questiontext.text:
Statement I: A real image formed by a converging optical system can be projected and captured on a physical screen placed at the image location.

Statement II: A virtual image formed by an optical system cannot be seen by the human eye under any circumstances.

कथन I: किसी अभिसारी प्रकाशिक निकाय द्वारा निर्मित वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब को प्रतिबिंब की स्थिति पर रखे भौतिक पर्दे पर प्रक्षेपित और प्राप्त किया जा सकता है।

कथन II: किसी प्रकाशिक निकाय द्वारा निर्मित आभासी प्रतिबिंब को किसी भी परिस्थिति में मानव नेत्र द्वारा नहीं देखा जा सकता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Real Images
A real image is formed by the actual physical convergence and intersection of reflected or refracted light rays. Because real photons pass through the focal points of the image space, placing a diffuse screen at that plane scatters the light, making the image visible on the screen. Therefore, the proposition regarding capturing a real image on a screen is completely valid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Virtual Images and Human Vision
A virtual image is formed at a point from which light rays appear to diverge; light rays do not actually intersect at the virtual image position, so it cannot be cast onto a screen. However, when these diverging rays enter a normal human eye, the eye's converging crystalline lens refracts them and focuses them to form a real image on the retina. Hence, virtual images (such as one's reflection in a plane mirror) are readily visible to the human eye. Therefore, the claim that virtual images can never be seen by the eye is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब का मूल्यांकन
वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब परावर्तित या अपवर्तित प्रकाश किरणों के वास्तविक भौतिक अभिसरण और प्रतिच्छेदन से बनता है। क्योंकि वास्तविक प्रकाश किरणें उस तल से होकर गुजरती हैं, इसलिए उस तल पर एक पर्दा रखने से प्रकाश प्रकीर्णित होता है और प्रतिबिंब पर्दे पर प्राप्त किया जा सकता है। अतः वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब को पर्दे पर प्राप्त करने संबंधी कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: आभासी प्रतिबिंब और मानव दृष्टि का मूल्यांकन
आभासी प्रतिबिंब उस बिंदु पर बनता है जहां से प्रकाश किरणें अपसरित होती हुई प्रतीत होती हैं; प्रकाश किरणें वास्तव में वहां प्रतिच्छेद नहीं करती हैं, इसलिए इसे पर्दे पर नहीं उतारा जा सकता। किंतु जब ये अपसारी किरणें मानव नेत्र में प्रवेश करती हैं, तो नेत्र का उत्तल लेंस इन्हें अपवर्तित करके रेटिना पर एक वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब बना देता है। इसी कारण हम समतल दर्पण में अपना आभासी प्रतिबिंब स्पष्ट देख पाते हैं। अतः आभासी प्रतिबिंब को कभी न देखे जा सकने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन सही है, जबकि दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q03 - Refraction frequency wavelength and refractive index

questiontext.text:
Statement I: When a monochromatic ray of light travels from air into a dense glass block, both its oscillation frequency and its wavelength remain strictly unchanged.

Statement II: The absolute refractive index of an optical medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in that medium.

कथन I: जब एकवर्णी प्रकाश किरण वायु से सघन कांच के गुटके में प्रवेश करती है, तो उसकी दोलन आवृत्ति और उसकी तरंगदैर्घ्य दोनों पूर्णतः अपरिवर्तित रहती हैं।

कथन II: किसी प्रकाशिक माध्यम का निरपेक्ष अपवर्तनांक निर्वात में प्रकाश की चाल और उस माध्यम में प्रकाश की चाल के अनुपात के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Frequency and Wavelength across Media
The frequency \(\nu\) of light is determined entirely by the oscillating source that creates the wave and does not change when passing across a stationary optical interface. However, the phase velocity of light decreases in a denser medium according to \(v = \frac{c}{n}\). Since the wave relationship is \(v = \nu \lambda\), the wavelength must decrease proportionally to \(\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{n}\). Therefore, the claim that both frequency and wavelength remain unchanged is scientifically incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of the Absolute Refractive Index Definition
By definition, the absolute refractive index \(n\) of any optical medium is given by the ratio of the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum \(c\) to the speed of light in that specific medium \(v\), expressed mathematically as \(n = \frac{c}{v}\). Because \(c > v\) in all conventional material media, \(n > 1\). This definition is exact and valid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: माध्यमों के पार आवृत्ति और तरंगदैर्घ्य का विश्लेषण
प्रकाश की आवृत्ति \(\nu\) पूर्णतः उस दोलनकारी स्रोत पर निर्भर करती है जो तरंग उत्पन्न करता है, और यह किसी स्थिर प्रकाशिक अंतरापृष्ठ को पार करने पर नहीं बदलती। किंतु सघन माध्यम में प्रकाश का वेग \(v = \frac{c}{n}\) के अनुसार घट जाता है। तरंग समीकरण \(v = \nu \lambda\) के अनुसार, तरंगदैर्घ्य भी घटकर \(\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{n}\) हो जाती है। अतः यह कथन कि आवृत्ति और तरंगदैर्घ्य दोनों अपरिवर्तित रहते हैं, गलत है।

चरण 2: निरपेक्ष अपवर्तनांक की परिभाषा का विश्लेषण
परिभाषा के अनुसार, किसी प्रकाशिक माध्यम का निरपेक्ष अपवर्तनांक \(n\), निर्वात में प्रकाश की चाल \(c\) और उस माध्यम में प्रकाश की चाल \(v\) का अनुपात होता है, जिसे गणितीय रूप से \(n = \frac{c}{v}\) लिखा जाता है। सभी सामान्य पदार्थों के लिए \(c > v\) होने के कारण \(n > 1\) होता है। यह परिभाषा पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन गलत है, जबकि दूसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q04 - Conditions for total internal reflection and diamond brilliance

questiontext.text:
Statement I: Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from an optically rarer medium toward an optically denser medium at angles exceeding the critical angle.

Statement II: The spectacular sparkle of a cut diamond is primarily due to its unusually large critical angle of approximately \(65^\circ\).

कथन I: पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन तब हो सकता है जब प्रकाश क्रांतिक कोण से अधिक कोण पर प्रकाशिक रूप से विरल माध्यम से सघन माध्यम की ओर गमन करता है।

कथन II: तराशे गए हीरे की शानदार चमक का मुख्य कारण इसका लगभग \(65^\circ\) का असामान्य रूप से बड़ा क्रांतिक कोण होना है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examination of Total Internal Reflection Conditions
Total internal reflection (TIR) requires two essential physical conditions: (i) light must travel from an optically denser medium toward an optically rarer medium, and (ii) the angle of incidence at the interface must exceed the critical angle \(i_c\). When light travels from a rarer medium into a denser medium, it always bends toward the normal and is transmitted into the medium for all physical incidence angles; total internal reflection can never occur in that direction. Thus, the condition stated in the first assertion is incorrect.

Step 2: Examination of Diamond Refractive Index and Critical Angle
Diamond has an exceptionally high refractive index of \(n \approx 2.42\). According to Snell's law at the critical boundary, \(\sin(i_c) = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{2.42} \approx 0.4132\), which yields a very small critical angle of \(i_c \approx 24.4^\circ\), rather than a large angle such as \(65^\circ\). Because the critical angle is remarkably small, rays entering a suitably cut diamond undergo multiple total internal reflections before exiting, producing its characteristic brilliance. Thus, the second assertion is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

चरण 1: पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन की शर्तों का परीक्षण
पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन (TIR) के लिए दो अनिवार्य शर्तें हैं: (i) प्रकाश को प्रकाशिक रूप से सघन माध्यम से विरल माध्यम की ओर जाना चाहिए, और (ii) आपतन कोण क्रांतिक कोण \(i_c\) से अधिक होना चाहिए। जब प्रकाश विरल से सघन माध्यम में जाता है, तो वह सदैव अभिलंब की ओर झुकता है और अपवर्तित होता है; उस दिशा में पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन कभी संभव नहीं है। अतः पहली बात गलत है।

चरण 2: हीरे के अपवर्तनांक और क्रांतिक कोण का परीक्षण
हीरे का अपवर्तनांक अत्यधिक उच्च (\(n \approx 2.42\)) होता है। क्रांतिक कोण के सूत्र \(\sin(i_c) = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{2.42} \approx 0.4132\) से क्रांतिक कोण का मान बहुत छोटा, लगभग \(i_c \approx 24.4^\circ\) प्राप्त होता है, न कि \(65^\circ\) जैसा कोई बड़ा मान। अत्यधिक छोटा क्रांतिक कोण होने के कारण हीरे में प्रवेश करने वाली किरणें कई बार पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तित होती हैं, जिससे चमक उत्पन्न होती है। अतः दूसरी बात भी गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q05 - Thin lens combinations and optical fiber transmission

questiontext.text:
Statement I: When two thin coaxial lenses of focal lengths \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) are kept in direct physical contact, the net optical power of the combination is equal to the algebraic sum of their individual powers.

Statement II: In an optical fiber, light signals propagate along the core by undergoing repeated total internal reflections at the core-cladding interface.

कथन I: जब फोकस दूरी \(f_1\) और \(f_2\) वाले दो पतले समाक्षीय लेंसों को सीधे भौतिक संपर्क में रखा जाता है, तो संयोजन की कुल प्रकाशिक क्षमता उनकी व्यक्तिगत क्षमताओं के बीजगणितीय योग के बराबर होती है।

कथन II: किसी प्रकाशिक फाइबर (ऑप्टिकल फाइबर) में, प्रकाश संकेत कोर-क्लैडिंग अंतरापृष्ठ पर बार-बार होने वाले पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तनों द्वारा कोर के अनुदिश संचरित होते हैं।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Lens Combination Power
For two thin lenses of focal lengths \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) in contact, the effective focal length \(F\) is given by \(\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}\). By definition, optical power is \(P = \frac{1}{f}\), which yields \(P = P_1 + P_2\). This algebraic sum correctly accounts for both positive (converging) and negative (diverging) lens powers.

Step 2: Analysis of Optical Fiber Waveguiding
An optical fiber consists of a central core of higher refractive index \(n_1\) surrounded by a cladding of slightly lower refractive index \(n_2\) (\(n_1 > n_2\)). When light enters the core within the acceptance cone, it strikes the core-cladding boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle, undergoing successive total internal reflections with negligible energy loss along the entire length of the fiber.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both principles are accurately stated and verified. Hence, both statements are correct.

चरण 1: लेंस संयोजन की क्षमता का विश्लेषण
संपर्क में रखे \(f_1\) और \(f_2\) फोकस दूरी वाले दो पतले लेंसों के लिए संयुक्त फोकस दूरी \(\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}\) होती है। प्रकाशिक क्षमता की परिभाषा \(P = \frac{1}{f}\) के अनुसार, कुल क्षमता \(P = P_1 + P_2\) होती है। यह बीजगणितीय योग उत्तल (धनात्मक) और अवतल (ऋणात्मक) दोनों प्रकार के लेंसों के लिए पूर्णतः मान्य है।

चरण 2: प्रकाशिक फाइबर में तरंग संचरण का विश्लेषण
ऑप्टिकल फाइबर में उच्च अपवर्तनांक \(n_1\) का एक केंद्रीय कोर होता है, जिसके चारों ओर थोड़े कम अपवर्तनांक \(n_2\) की क्लैडिंग होती है (\(n_1 > n_2\))। जब प्रकाश उपयुक्त कोण पर कोर में प्रवेश करता है, तो यह कोर-क्लैडिंग सीमा पर क्रांतिक कोण से बड़े कोण पर टकराता है और न्यूनतम ऊर्जा क्षय के साथ निरंतर पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तित होकर आगे बढ़ता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
दोनों सिद्धांतों का निरूपण पूर्णतः सही है। अतः दोनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q06 - Minimum deviation in prism and lens combination magnification

questiontext.text:
Statement I: At the condition of minimum deviation for an equilateral glass prism, the refracted ray inside the prism travels parallel to the base of the prism.

Statement II: The net linear magnification produced by two thin coaxial lenses in contact is equal to the algebraic sum of their individual magnifications.

कथन I: एक समबाहु कांच के प्रिज्म के लिए न्यूनतम विचलन की स्थिति में, प्रिज्म के भीतर अपवर्तित किरण प्रिज्म के आधार के समांतर गमन करती है।

कथन II: संपर्क में रखे दो पतले समाक्षीय लेंसों द्वारा उत्पन्न कुल रैखिक आवर्धन उनके व्यक्तिगत आवर्धनों के बीजगणितीय योग के बराबर होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Ray Path at Minimum Deviation
At minimum deviation \(D = D_m\), the light ray passes through a symmetrical triangular prism symmetrically, so that the angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence (\(i = e\)) and the internal refraction angles are equal (\(r_1 = r_2 = \frac{A}{2}\)). By symmetry, the refracted ray inside the prism is strictly parallel to the base of the prism. Therefore, this assertion is physically correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Total Magnification of Lens Combinations
When two thin lenses are placed in contact, the image formed by the first lens acts as the object for the second lens. If the first lens produces linear magnification \(m_1 = \frac{h'}{h}\) and the second produces \(m_2 = \frac{h''}{h'}\), the overall magnification is \(m = \frac{h''}{h} = \left(\frac{h''}{h'}\right) \left(\frac{h'}{h}\right) = m_1 \times m_2\). Magnifications multiply rather than add. Therefore, asserting that net magnification is the algebraic sum is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: न्यूनतम विचलन पर किरण पथ का मूल्यांकन
न्यूनतम विचलन (\(D = D_m\)) की स्थिति में, किरण सममित प्रिज्म से सममित रूप से गुजरती है, जिससे आपतन कोण और निर्गत कोण बराबर होते हैं (\(i = e\)) तथा प्रिज्म के भीतर अपवर्तन कोण भी समान होते हैं (\(r_1 = r_2 = \frac{A}{2}\))। सममिति के कारण प्रिज्म के अंदर अपवर्तित किरण आधार के ठीक समांतर हो जाती है। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: लेंस संयोजनों के कुल आवर्धन का मूल्यांकन
जब दो पतले लेंस संपर्क में होते हैं, तो पहले लेंस द्वारा बनाया गया प्रतिबिंब दूसरे लेंस के लिए वस्तु का कार्य करता है। यदि पहले लेंस का रैखिक आवर्धन \(m_1\) और दूसरे का \(m_2\) है, तो कुल आवर्धन दोनों के गुणनफल के बराबर होता है, अर्थात \(m = m_1 \times m_2\)। आवर्धन जुड़ते नहीं हैं बल्कि गुणा होते हैं। अतः कुल आवर्धन को बीजगणितीय योग बताना गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन सही है, जबकि दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q07 - Design parameters of astronomical telescope and compound microscope

questiontext.text:
Statement I: In an astronomical refracting telescope, the objective lens must have a small focal length and a small aperture, while the eyepiece must have a very large focal length.

Statement II: In a compound microscope, both the objective lens and the eyepiece should have small focal lengths to achieve a high overall angular magnification.

कथन I: किसी खगोलीय अपवर्ती दूरदर्शक में, अभिदृश्यक लेंस की फोकस दूरी और द्वारक दोनों छोटे होने चाहिए, जबकि नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी बहुत बड़ी होनी चाहिए।

कथन II: किसी संयुक्त सूक्ष्मदर्शी में, उच्च कुल कोणीय आवर्धन प्राप्त करने के लिए अभिदृश्यक लेंस और नेत्रिका दोनों की फोकस दूरियां छोटी होनी चाहिए।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of the Astronomical Telescope Design
The angular magnification of an astronomical refracting telescope in normal adjustment is given by \(m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\), where \(f_o\) is the objective focal length and \(f_e\) is the eyepiece focal length. To achieve high angular magnification and high resolving power, the objective lens must have a very large focal length (\(f_o \gg f_e\)) and a large aperture to gather sufficient light from distant celestial objects. The eyepiece must have a comparatively short focal length. The assertion stating that the objective requires a small focal length and aperture is completely backward and incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of the Compound Microscope Design
The total angular magnification of a compound microscope is given by \(m \approx \left(\frac{L}{f_o}\right)\left(1 + \frac{D}{f_e}\right)\) for normal adjustment, where \(L\) is the tube length, \(D\) is the near point distance, \(f_o\) is the focal length of the objective, and \(f_e\) is the focal length of the eyepiece. Because both \(f_o\) and \(f_e\) appear in the denominators, both lenses must possess small focal lengths to maximize the total magnification. Thus, this assertion is physically accurate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: खगोलीय दूरदर्शक की बनावट का विश्लेषण
सामान्य समायोजन में खगोलीय अपवर्ती दूरदर्शक का कोणीय आवर्धन \(m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\) होता है, जहाँ \(f_o\) अभिदृश्यक की फोकस दूरी और \(f_e\) नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी है। उच्च आवर्धन और उच्च विभेदन क्षमता प्राप्त करने के लिए, अभिदृश्यक लेंस की फोकस दूरी बहुत बड़ी (\(f_o \gg f_e\)) तथा दूरस्थ खगोलीय पिंडों से पर्याप्त प्रकाश एकत्र करने के लिए इसका द्वारक भी बड़ा होना चाहिए। नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी छोटी होनी चाहिए। अतः अभिदृश्यक की फोकस दूरी और द्वारक को छोटा बताने वाला कथन पूर्णतः गलत है।

चरण 2: संयुक्त सूक्ष्मदर्शी की बनावट का विश्लेषण
संयुक्त सूक्ष्मदर्शी का कुल कोणीय आवर्धन \(m \approx \left(\frac{L}{f_o}\right)\left(1 + \frac{D}{f_e}\right)\) सूत्र द्वारा दिया जाता है, जहाँ \(L\) नली की लंबाई, \(D\) स्पष्ट दृष्टि की न्यूनतम दूरी, \(f_o\) अभिदृश्यक की फोकस दूरी तथा \(f_e\) नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी है। चूँकि \(f_o\) और \(f_e\) दोनों हर (डिनॉमिनेटर) में आते हैं, इसलिए उच्च आवर्धन प्राप्त करने के लिए दोनों लेंसों की फोकस दूरियाँ छोटी होनी चाहिए। अतः यह कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन गलत है, जबकि दूसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT_Q08 - Chromatic aberration and Cassegrain reflector mirrors

questiontext.text:
Statement I: Mirrors employed in reflecting telescopes are inherently free from chromatic aberration because the law of reflection does not depend on the wavelength of light.

Statement II: In a Cassegrain reflecting telescope, the secondary mirror positioned to reflect rays toward the central opening in the primary parabolic mirror is a concave mirror.

कथन I: परावर्ती दूरदर्शकों में प्रयुक्त दर्पण स्वभाविक रूप से वर्ण विपथन (क्रोमैटिक एबरेशन) से मुक्त होते हैं क्योंकि परावर्तन का नियम प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य पर निर्भर नहीं करता है।

कथन II: कैसेग्रेन परावर्ती दूरदर्शक में, प्राथमिक परवलयिक दर्पण के केंद्रीय छिद्र की ओर किरणों को परावर्तित करने के लिए स्थापित द्वितीयक दर्पण एक अवतल दर्पण होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Chromatic Aberration in Mirrors
Chromatic aberration in lenses arises from material dispersion, where refractive index varies with wavelength (\(n = n(\lambda)\)), causing different colors to converge at different focal points. In contrast, reflection of light at a metallic or silvered mirror surface depends strictly on the law of reflection (\(i = r\)), which is completely independent of wavelength. Consequently, all wavelengths focus at identical points, making mirror-based reflecting systems completely free from chromatic aberration. This makes the first statement scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Mirror Configuration in a Cassegrain Telescope
A Cassegrain reflecting telescope employs a large concave (typically paraboloidal) primary mirror that collects incoming parallel rays and converges them toward its primary focus. Before the rays reach this focal point, they strike a secondary mirror that redirects them through a small central hole in the primary mirror to an eyepiece. Crucially, this secondary mirror is a convex mirror, not a concave mirror. Therefore, the assertion claiming the secondary mirror is concave is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: दर्पणों में वर्ण विपथन का मूल्यांकन
लेंसों में वर्ण विपथन (क्रोमैटिक एबरेशन) माध्यम के परिक्षेपण के कारण होता है, जहाँ अपवर्तनांक तरंगदैर्घ्य पर निर्भर करता है (\(n = n(\lambda)\)), जिससे विभिन्न रंग अलग-अलग बिंदुओं पर केंद्रित होते हैं। इसके विपरीत, दर्पणों पर परावर्तन केवल परावर्तन के नियम (\(i = r\)) का पालन करता है, जो प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य पर बिल्कुल निर्भर नहीं करता। अतः सभी रंग एक ही बिंदु पर केंद्रित होते हैं और दर्पण वर्ण विपथन से सर्वथा मुक्त होते हैं। यह कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: कैसेग्रेन दूरदर्शक में दर्पणों के विन्यास का मूल्यांकन
कैसेग्रेन परावर्ती दूरदर्शक में एक बड़ा अवतल (परवलयिक) प्राथमिक दर्पण होता है जो दूर से आने वाली किरणों को अभिसरित करता है। इन किरणों के प्राथमिक फोकस पर मिलने से पहले ही, एक द्वितीयक दर्पण द्वारा उन्हें प्राथमिक दर्पण के केंद्र में बने छिद्र की ओर परावर्तित कर दिया जाता है। अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण तथ्य यह है कि यह द्वितीयक दर्पण एक उत्तल दर्पण होता है, अवतल नहीं। अतः द्वितीयक दर्पण को अवतल बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन सही है, जबकि दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Laws of reflection and spherical mirror image formation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding spherical mirrors:

Statement I: The laws of reflection are valid at each point of a curved reflecting surface just as they are for a plane surface.

Statement II: For a concave mirror of small aperture, the focal length is equal to half of its radius of curvature under paraxial approximation.

Statement III: A convex mirror always forms a real and inverted image of an object placed in front of it along the principal axis.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

गोलीय दर्पणों के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: परावर्तन के नियम किसी वक्र परावर्तक सतह के प्रत्येक बिंदु पर उसी प्रकार मान्य होते हैं जैसे वे समतल सतह के लिए होते हैं।

कथन II: छोटे द्वारक वाले अवतल दर्पण के लिए, उपाक्षीय सन्निकटन के तहत फोकस दूरी उसकी वक्रता त्रिज्या के आधे के बराबर होती है।

कथन III: एक उत्तल दर्पण मुख्य अक्ष पर अपने सामने रखी वस्तु का सदैव एक वास्तविक और उल्टा प्रतिबिंब बनाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Laws of Reflection on Curved Surfaces
The fundamental laws of reflection—that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection and that the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane—hold strictly at each local point on any reflective boundary, whether planar or spherical. The normal at any point on a spherical mirror is along the radius connecting that point to the center of curvature. Hence, the assertion regarding reflection on curved boundaries is valid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Paraxial Focal Length Relationship
For paraxial rays striking a spherical mirror of small aperture, geometric analysis shows that rays parallel to the principal axis converge at (or appear to diverge from) a focal point \(F\) such that \(f = \frac{R}{2}\). Hence, the assertion stating that the focal length equals half the radius of curvature is valid.

Step 3: Evaluation of Image Formation by a Convex Mirror
For any real object positioned at any distance in front of a convex mirror, the reflected rays diverge. When projected backwards, these rays intersect behind the mirror between the pole and the principal focus. Consequently, a convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image of a real object, never a real or inverted image. Hence, the assertion claiming real and inverted image formation by a convex mirror is invalid.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the principles regarding the validity of reflection laws and the paraxial focal length relation are correct, while the claim regarding real image formation by a convex mirror is incorrect.

चरण 1: वक्र सतहों पर परावर्तन के नियमों का मूल्यांकन
परावर्तन के मूलभूत नियम—आपतन कोण परावर्तन कोण के बराबर होता है तथा आपतित किरण, परावर्तित किरण और अभिलंब एक ही तल में स्थित होते हैं—समतल या गोलीय किसी भी परावर्तक सतह के प्रत्येक स्थानीय बिंदु पर पूर्णतः मान्य होते हैं। गोलीय दर्पण के किसी भी बिंदु पर अभिलंब उस बिंदु को वक्रता केंद्र से मिलाने वाली त्रिज्या के अनुदिश होता है। अतः वक्र सतहों पर परावर्तन संबंधी कथन सही है।

चरण 2: उपाक्षीय फोकस दूरी संबंध का मूल्यांकन
छोटे द्वारक वाले गोलीय दर्पण पर आपतित उपाक्षीय किरणों के लिए, ज्यामितीय विश्लेषण से यह सिद्ध होता है कि मुख्य अक्ष के समांतर किरणें फोकस बिंदु \(F\) पर अभिसरित होती हैं (या वहां से अपसरित होती प्रतीत होती हैं), जिससे \(f = \frac{R}{2}\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः फोकस दूरी के वक्रता त्रिज्या के आधे होने संबंधी कथन सही है।

चरण 3: उत्तल दर्पण द्वारा प्रतिबिंब निर्माण का मूल्यांकन
उत्तल दर्पण के सामने किसी भी दूरी पर रखी वास्तविक वस्तु के लिए, परावर्तित किरणें अपसरित होती हैं। पीछे बढ़ाने पर ये किरणें दर्पण के पीछे ध्रुव और मुख्य फोकस के बीच मिलती हैं। फलस्वरूप, उत्तल दर्पण किसी वास्तविक वस्तु का सदैव आभासी, सीधा और छोटा प्रतिबिंब बनाता है, कभी भी वास्तविक या उल्टा प्रतिबिंब नहीं बनाता। अतः उत्तल दर्पण द्वारा वास्तविक और उल्टे प्रतिबिंब निर्माण का दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल परावर्तन के नियमों की वैधता और उपाक्षीय फोकस दूरी संबंध ही सही हैं, जबकि उत्तल दर्पण द्वारा वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब बनने का दावा गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Wave properties of refracted light optical density and apparent depth

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding refraction of light:

Statement I: When light passes from air into a denser transparent medium, its frequency decreases proportionally with its speed.

Statement II: Optical density of an optical medium is not necessarily identical to its mass density; for example, turpentine has a lower mass density than water but possesses a higher optical density.

Statement III: When an object immersed in water is viewed from air nearly normally, its apparent depth is less than its real depth due to refraction at the interface.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

प्रकाश के अपवर्तन के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: जब प्रकाश वायु से किसी सघन पारदर्शी माध्यम में प्रवेश करता है, तो उसकी आवृत्ति उसकी चाल के अनुपात में घट जाती है।

कथन II: किसी प्रकाशिक माध्यम का प्रकाशिक घनत्व उसके द्रव्यमान घनत्व के समरूप होना अनिवार्य नहीं है; उदाहरण के लिए, तारपीन का द्रव्यमान घनत्व जल से कम होता है किंतु इसका प्रकाशिक घनत्व अधिक होता है।

कथन III: जब जल में डूबी किसी वस्तु को वायु से लगभग अभिलंबवत देखा जाता है, तो अंतरापृष्ठ पर अपवर्तन के कारण इसकी आभासी गहराई इसकी वास्तविक गहराई से कम होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Wave Frequency during Refraction
The frequency \(\nu\) of light depends solely on the oscillating source that emits the electromagnetic radiation. When light traverses a stationary boundary between two media, the frequency remains strictly constant. The decrease in wave speed \(v = \frac{c}{n}\) is accommodated entirely by a proportional decrease in wavelength \(\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{n}\). Therefore, the claim that frequency decreases is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Optical Density versus Mass Density
Optical density measures the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to that in the medium (refractive index), whereas mass density represents mass per unit volume. They are independent physical quantities. Turpentine floats on water because its mass density is lower than that of water, yet its refractive index (\(n \approx 1.47\)) is higher than that of water (\(n \approx 1.33\)), making it optically denser. Thus, this assertion is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Apparent Depth
Rays originating from an object immersed in a denser medium bend away from the normal upon emerging into air. For near-normal viewing, the virtual rays appear to diverge from a shallower depth given by \(h_{\text{apparent}} = \frac{h_{\text{real}}}{n}\). Because \(n > 1\), the apparent depth is always less than the real depth. Thus, this assertion is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The assertion regarding frequency change is incorrect, whereas the assertions concerning the distinction between optical and mass density and the reduction in apparent depth are correct.

चरण 1: अपवर्तन के दौरान तरंग आवृत्ति का मूल्यांकन
प्रकाश की आवृत्ति \(\nu\) केवल उस दोलनकारी स्रोत पर निर्भर करती है जो विद्युत चुंबकीय विकिरण उत्सर्जित करता है। जब प्रकाश दो माध्यमों के स्थिर अंतरापृष्ठ को पार करता है, तो आवृत्ति पूर्णतः नियत रहती है। माध्यम में प्रकाश की चाल घटने (\(v = \frac{c}{n}\)) पर तरंगदैर्घ्य समानुपाती रूप से घटती है (\(\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{n}\))। अतः आवृत्ति घटने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 2: प्रकाशिक घनत्व बनाम द्रव्यमान घनत्व का मूल्यांकन
प्रकाशिक घनत्व माध्यम के अपवर्तनांक (निर्वात में चाल और माध्यम में चाल के अनुपात) से संबंधित है, जबकि द्रव्यमान घनत्व प्रति इकाई आयतन द्रव्यमान होता है। ये दोनों स्वतंत्र भौतिक राशियां हैं। तारपीन का तेल जल पर तैरता है क्योंकि इसका द्रव्यमान घनत्व जल से कम है, किंतु इसका अपवर्तनांक (\(n \approx 1.47\)) जल (\(n \approx 1.33\)) से अधिक है, अतः यह अधिक प्रकाशिक सघन है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: आभासी गहराई का मूल्यांकन
सघन माध्यम में स्थित वस्तु से चलने वाली किरणें वायु में प्रवेश करते समय अभिलंब से दूर झुक जाती हैं। अभिलंबवत देखने पर किरणें कम गहराई से आती प्रतीत होती हैं, जिसका मान \(h_{\text{apparent}} = \frac{h_{\text{real}}}{n}\) होता है। \(n > 1\) होने के कारण आभासी गहराई सदैव वास्तविक गहराई से कम होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
आवृत्ति में परिवर्तन संबंधी कथन गलत है, जबकि प्रकाशिक व द्रव्यमान घनत्व के अंतर तथा आभासी गहराई संबंधी कथन सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Conditions and applications of total internal reflection

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding total internal reflection:

Statement I: Total internal reflection occurs only when light attempts to pass from an optically denser medium into an optically rarer medium at an angle of incidence exceeding the critical angle.

Statement II: In an optical fiber, light propagates efficiently along the central core because the refractive index of the core material is strictly greater than that of the outer cladding.

Statement III: Diamond exhibits exceptional brilliance primarily because its high refractive index yields an exceptionally small critical angle of approximately \(24.4^\circ\), causing multiple internal reflections.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन केवल तभी घटित होता है जब प्रकाश प्रकाशिक रूप से सघन माध्यम से विरल माध्यम में क्रांतिक कोण से अधिक आपतन कोण पर प्रवेश करने का प्रयास करता है।

कथन II: प्रकाशिक फाइबर (ऑप्टिकल फाइबर) में प्रकाश केंद्रीय कोर के अनुदिश दक्षतापूर्वक संचरित होता है क्योंकि कोर पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक बाहरी क्लैडिंग की तुलना में निश्चित रूप से अधिक होता है।

कथन III: हीरा मुख्य रूप से इसलिए असाधारण चमक प्रदर्शित करता है क्योंकि इसका उच्च अपवर्तनांक लगभग \(24.4^\circ\) का अत्यधिक छोटा क्रांतिक कोण प्रदान करता है, जिससे कई आंतरिक परावर्तन होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Physical Conditions for Total Internal Reflection
Total internal reflection occurs exclusively when two conditions are simultaneously satisfied: light must travel from an optically denser medium toward an optically rarer medium, and the angle of incidence at the boundary must exceed the critical angle defined by \(\sin(i_c) = \frac{n_2}{n_1}\). When these criteria are met, no refracted ray is transmitted, and the entire incident wave energy is internally reflected. Hence, this assertion is completely valid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Optical Fiber Core and Cladding Design
Optical fibers are engineered with a central cylindrical core of refractive index \(n_1\) surrounded by a cladding layer of slightly lower refractive index \(n_2\) (\(n_1 > n_2\)). Light launched into the core strikes the core-cladding boundary at angles greater than the critical angle, undergoing successive lossless total internal reflections that guide the signal along the fiber. Hence, this assertion is completely valid.

Step 3: Evaluation of Diamond Brilliance and Critical Angle
Diamond has an exceptionally large refractive index of \(n \approx 2.42\). From \(\sin(i_c) = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{2.42}\), the critical angle is remarkably small at \(i_c \approx 24.4^\circ\). Expertly cut facets ensure that light entering the top face strikes internal boundaries at angles exceeding \(24.4^\circ\), undergoing repeated internal reflections before emerging, producing its sparkling brilliance. Hence, this assertion is completely valid.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All three physical assertions concerning total internal reflection conditions, optical fiber architecture, and diamond brilliance are accurate and well-substantiated.

चरण 1: पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन की भौतिक शर्तों का मूल्यांकन
पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन केवल तभी होता है जब दो शर्तें एक साथ पूरी हों: प्रकाश को सघन माध्यम से विरल माध्यम की ओर जाना चाहिए, तथा अंतरापृष्ठ पर आपतन कोण क्रांतिक कोण (\(\sin(i_c) = \frac{n_2}{n_1}\)) से अधिक होना चाहिए। इन शर्तों के पूरा होने पर कोई अपवर्तित किरण बाहर नहीं निकलती और संपूर्ण प्रकाश ऊर्जा परावर्तित हो जाती है। अतः यह कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: प्रकाशिक फाइबर के कोर और क्लैडिंग की बनावट का मूल्यांकन
ऑप्टिकल फाइबर में उच्च अपवर्तनांक \(n_1\) का एक केंद्रीय कोर होता है, जिसके चारों ओर कम अपवर्तनांक \(n_2\) की क्लैडिंग होती है (\(n_1 > n_2\))। कोर में प्रवेश करने वाला प्रकाश कोर-क्लैडिंग सीमा पर क्रांतिक कोण से बड़े कोण पर टकराता है और ऊर्जा की हानि के बिना लगातार पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तित होकर आगे बढ़ता है। अतः यह कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: हीरे की चमक और क्रांतिक कोण का मूल्यांकन
हीरे का अपवर्तनांक अत्यधिक उच्च (\(n \approx 2.42\)) होता है। सूत्र \(\sin(i_c) = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{1}{2.42}\) से इसका क्रांतिक कोण बहुत छोटा, लगभग \(i_c \approx 24.4^\circ\) प्राप्त होता है। तराशे गए फलकों के कारण अंदर प्रवेश करने वाला प्रकाश बार-बार पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तित होता है, जिससे शानदार चमक उत्पन्न होती है। अतः यह कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पूर्ण आंतरिक परावर्तन की शर्तों, प्रकाशिक फाइबर की बनावट और हीरे की चमक से संबंधित तीनों कथन पूर्णतः सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_CH09_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Lens combinations and telescope optical configurations

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding lens systems and telescopes:

Statement I: When two thin coaxial lenses of focal lengths \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) are placed in direct contact, the net optical power of the combination equals the algebraic sum of their individual powers.

Statement II: In an astronomical refracting telescope, the objective lens must have a small focal length and small aperture compared to the eyepiece to maximize angular magnification.

Statement III: In a Cassegrain reflecting telescope, the secondary mirror that reflects converging rays through a central aperture in the primary paraboloidal mirror is a convex mirror.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

लेंस निकायों और दूरदर्शकों के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: जब फोकस दूरी \(f_1\) और \(f_2\) वाले दो पतले समाक्षीय लेंसों को सीधे संपर्क में रखा जाता है, तो संयोजन की कुल प्रकाशिक क्षमता उनकी व्यक्तिगत क्षमताओं के बीजगणितीय योग के बराबर होती है।

कथन II: किसी खगोलीय अपवर्ती दूरदर्शक में, कोणीय आवर्धन को अधिकतम करने के लिए अभिदृश्यक लेंस की फोकस दूरी और द्वारक दोनों नेत्रिका की तुलना में छोटे होने चाहिए।

कथन III: कैसेग्रेन परावर्ती दूरदर्शक में, प्राथमिक परवलयिक दर्पण के केंद्रीय छिद्र से अभिसारी किरणों को परावर्तित करने वाला द्वितीयक दर्पण एक उत्तल दर्पण होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Lens Combination Power
For two thin lenses in contact, their focal lengths combine according to \(\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}\). By definition, optical power is \(P = \frac{1}{f}\), which directly yields \(P = P_1 + P_2\). Because converging lenses have positive power and diverging lenses have negative power, the net power is precisely the algebraic sum of individual powers. Hence, this assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Astronomical Telescope Optics
The angular magnifying power of an astronomical refracting telescope in normal adjustment is \(m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\), where \(f_o\) is the objective focal length and \(f_e\) is the eyepiece focal length. To achieve high magnification as well as high resolving power and light gathering ability, the objective must have a very large focal length and a large aperture, while the eyepiece requires a short focal length. The assertion stating that the objective has a small focal length and aperture is completely inverted and incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cassegrain Telescope Construction
In a Cassegrain reflecting telescope, light from distant astronomical bodies is collected and converged by a large concave paraboloidal primary mirror. Before reaching the primary focus, the convergent beam strikes a secondary mirror that directs the rays back through a hole in the center of the primary mirror to the eyepiece. In this optical layout, the secondary mirror is specifically a convex mirror. Hence, this assertion is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The assertions regarding the net power of thin lenses in contact and the convex secondary mirror of a Cassegrain telescope are correct, whereas the assertion regarding the objective parameters of an astronomical telescope is incorrect.

चरण 1: संपर्क में रखे लेंसों की कुल क्षमता का मूल्यांकन
संपर्क में रखे दो पतले लेंसों के लिए संयुक्त फोकस दूरी \(\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}\) होती है। लेंस की क्षमता \(P = \frac{1}{f}\) होने के कारण कुल क्षमता \(P = P_1 + P_2\) प्राप्त होती है। चूंकि उत्तल लेंस की क्षमता धनात्मक तथा अवतल लेंस की क्षमता ऋणात्मक होती है, इसलिए कुल क्षमता व्यक्तिगत क्षमताओं का बीजगणितीय योग होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: खगोलीय दूरदर्शक के प्रकाशिक घटकों का मूल्यांकन
सामान्य समायोजन में खगोलीय अपवर्ती दूरदर्शक की कोणीय आवर्धन क्षमता \(m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\) होती है, जहाँ \(f_o\) अभिदृश्यक की फोकस दूरी और \(f_e\) नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी है। उच्च आवर्धन, उच्च विभेदन और अधिक प्रकाश एकत्र करने के लिए, अभिदृश्यक लेंस की फोकस दूरी और द्वारक दोनों बहुत बड़े होने चाहिए, जबकि नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी छोटी होनी चाहिए। अतः अभिदृश्यक की फोकस दूरी और द्वारक को छोटा बताने वाला दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: कैसेग्रेन दूरदर्शक की बनावट का मूल्यांकन
कैसेग्रेन परावर्ती दूरदर्शक में, एक बड़ा अवतल परवलयिक प्राथमिक दर्पण प्रकाश को अभिसरित करता है। किरणों के प्राथमिक फोकस पर मिलने से पहले ही, एक द्वितीयक दर्पण द्वारा उन्हें प्राथमिक दर्पण के केंद्रीय छिद्र की ओर मोड़ दिया जाता है। इस व्यवस्था में प्रयुक्त द्वितीयक दर्पण एक उत्तल दर्पण होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
संपर्क में रखे लेंसों की क्षमता और कैसेग्रेन दूरदर्शक में उत्तल द्वितीयक दर्पण संबंधी कथन सही हैं, जबकि खगोलीय दूरदर्शक के अभिदृश्यक संबंधी कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_MATCH_Q01 - Image formation by a concave mirror

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Object Position for Concave Mirror)List II (Image Position and Characteristics)
A. At infinityI. At \(C\), real, inverted, and same size
B. Beyond \(C\)II. At \(F\), real, inverted, and highly diminished
C. At centre of curvature \(C\)III. Behind mirror, virtual, erect, and magnified
D. Between focus \(F\) and pole \(P\)IV. Between \(F\) and \(C\), real, inverted, and diminished

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For a concave spherical mirror of focal length \(f\) and radius of curvature \(R = 2f\), the mirror equation \(\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\) and linear magnification formula \(m = -\frac{v}{u}\) dictate the position, nature, and size of the image formed for different object locations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Item A
When the object is at infinity (\(u \to -\infty\)), incident rays are parallel to the principal axis and converge at the principal focus after reflection (\(v = f\)). The image is formed at \(F\), and is real, inverted, and highly diminished point-like. This matches II.

Step 3: Evaluation of Item B
When the object is placed beyond the centre of curvature \(C\) (\(|u| > 2|f|\)), the image distance satisfies \(|f| < |v| < 2|f|\). Hence, the image is formed between \(F\) and \(C\), and is real, inverted, and diminished. This matches IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of Item C
When the object is placed exactly at the centre of curvature \(C\) (\(u = -2f\)), the image is also formed at \(C\) (\(v = -2f\)), with magnification \(m = -\frac{-2f}{-2f} = -1\). The image is real, inverted, and of the exact same size as the object. This matches I.

Step 5: Evaluation of Item D
When the object is placed between the focus \(F\) and the pole \(P\) (\(|u| < |f|\)), the reflected rays diverge and appear to intersect behind the reflecting surface (\(v > 0\)). The image is virtual, erect, and magnified (\(m > +1\)). This matches III.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct pairwise matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

Final Answer:
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_MATCH_Q02 - Critical angles of optical media

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Transparent Substance)List II (Critical Angle with Respect to Air)
A. Water (\(n = 1.33\))I. \(24.41^\circ\)
B. Crown glass (\(n = 1.52\))II. \(48.75^\circ\)
C. Dense flint glass (\(n = 1.62\))III. \(37.31^\circ\)
D. Diamond (\(n = 2.42\))IV. \(41.14^\circ\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The critical angle \(i_c\) for an optical medium of refractive index \(n\) relative to air (\(n_{\text{air}} \approx 1\)) is given by Snell's law when the angle of refraction is \(90^\circ\): \[\sin i_c = \frac{1}{n} \implies i_c = \arcsin\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)\] As the refractive index \(n\) increases, the critical angle \(i_c\) becomes correspondingly smaller.

Step 2: Evaluation of Item A
For water, \(n = 1.33\). The critical angle is \(\sin i_c = \frac{1}{1.33} \approx 0.7519\), giving \(i_c \approx 48.75^\circ\). This matches II.

Step 3: Evaluation of Item B
For crown glass, \(n = 1.52\). The critical angle is \(\sin i_c = \frac{1}{1.52} \approx 0.6579\), giving \(i_c \approx 41.14^\circ\). This matches IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of Item C
For dense flint glass, \(n = 1.62\). The critical angle is \(\sin i_c = \frac{1}{1.62} \approx 0.6173\), giving \(i_c \approx 37.31^\circ\). This matches III.

Step 5: Evaluation of Item D
For diamond, \(n = 2.42\). The critical angle is \(\sin i_c = \frac{1}{2.42} \approx 0.4132\), giving \(i_c \approx 24.41^\circ\). This matches I.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct pairwise matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Final Answer:
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_MATCH_Q03 - Formulae for refraction and lenses

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Optical Relation / Law)List II (Mathematical Expression)
A. Thin lens formulaI. \(m = \frac{v}{u}\)
B. Lens maker\'s formula (in air)II. \(\frac{n_2}{v} - \frac{n_1}{u} = \frac{n_2 - n_1}{R}\)
C. Linear magnification of a lensIII. \(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\)
D. Refraction at a single spherical surfaceIV. \(\frac{1}{f} = (n - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Geometrical ray optics establishes standard mathematical relationships connecting object distance \(u\), image distance \(v\), radii of curvature \(R\), refractive indices \(n\), and focal length \(f\) under the paraxial ray approximation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Item A
The thin lens formula relates the object distance \(u\), image distance \(v\), and focal length \(f\) of a thin spherical lens as: \[\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}\] This corresponds to III.

Step 3: Evaluation of Item B
The Lens Maker's formula relates the focal length \(f\) of a lens to the refractive index \(n\) of its material and the radii of curvature \(R_1, R_2\) of its refracting surfaces in air: \[\frac{1}{f} = (n - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)\] This corresponds to IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of Item C
Linear magnification \(m\) produced by a spherical lens is defined as the ratio of image height to object height, which simplifies geometrically to: \[m = \frac{h'}{h} = \frac{v}{u}\] This corresponds to I.

Step 5: Evaluation of Item D
Refraction at a single spherical surface of radius of curvature \(R\) separating a medium of refractive index \(n_1\) from a medium of refractive index \(n_2\) is governed by: \[\frac{n_2}{v} - \frac{n_1}{u} = \frac{n_2 - n_1}{R}\] This corresponds to II.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct pairwise matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Final Answer:
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_MATCH_Q04 - Optical instruments and magnifying power

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Optical Device and Operating Condition)List II (Magnifying Power Formula / Design Feature)
A. Simple microscope with image at near point \(D\)I. Uses a parabolic concave primary mirror and a convex secondary mirror
B. Simple microscope with image at infinityII. Magnification \(m = 1 + \frac{D}{f}\)
C. Astronomical telescope in normal adjustmentIII. Angular magnification \(m = \frac{D}{f}\)
D. Cassegrain reflecting telescopeIV. Magnifying power \(m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\) with tube length \(L = f_o + f_e\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Optical instruments provide angular magnification to facilitate clear observation of minute or distant objects. Magnifying power depends on the focal lengths of the constituent optical elements and the location of the final image (at the near point \(D \approx 25\text{ cm}\) or at infinity for relaxed eye viewing).

Step 2: Evaluation of Item A
A simple microscope consists of a single converging lens of short focal length \(f\). When the object is positioned such that the virtual, erect image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision \(D\), the linear magnification is \(m = \frac{v}{u} = 1 - \frac{v}{f}\). With \(v = -D\), this yields: \[m = 1 + \frac{D}{f}\] This matches II.

Step 3: Evaluation of Item B
When the object is placed at the principal focus of the magnifying lens, the virtual image is formed at infinity for relaxed eye observation. The angular magnification is the ratio of the angle subtended by the image to the angle subtended by the object at the near point without a lens: \[m = \frac{\theta_i}{\theta_o} = \frac{D}{f}\] This matches III.

Step 4: Evaluation of Item C
An astronomical refracting telescope in normal adjustment forms the final image at infinity. Its magnifying power is the ratio of the angle subtended by the image to that subtended by the distant object: \[m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\] The separation between the objective lens and eyepiece is the sum of their focal lengths, \(L = f_o + f_e\). This matches IV.

Step 5: Evaluation of Item D
A Cassegrain telescope is a reflecting telescope design that employs a large concave primary mirror with a central hole to collect light and a smaller convex secondary mirror to reflect convergent rays through the hole to the eyepiece. This matches I.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct pairwise matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Final Answer:
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Rotation of reflected ray by plane mirror

questiontext.text: A light ray is incident on a plane mirror. If the plane mirror is rotated by an angle of \(15^\circ\) about an axis lying in the plane of the mirror and perpendicular to the plane of incidence, by what angle does the reflected ray rotate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Angle of rotation of the plane mirror: \(\theta = 15^\circ\). The rotation axis lies in the plane of the mirror and is perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The direction of the incident ray remains fixed. Angles are measured in the plane of incidence.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
When a reflecting surface rotates by an angle \(\theta\) while keeping the incident ray fixed, the normal to the mirror rotates by \(\theta\), and the reflected ray turns through twice that angle: \[\Delta \theta_{\text{reflected}} = 2\theta\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given rotation angle into the formula: \[\Delta \theta_{\text{reflected}} = 2 \times 15^\circ = 30^\circ\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The doubling of angular deflection for reflected light is consistent with the law of reflection \(i = r\). The reflected ray turns through \(30^\circ\).

Final Answer:
The reflected ray rotates by \(30^\circ\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Focal length of concave spherical mirror

questiontext.text: A concave spherical mirror has a radius of curvature of \(30\text{ cm}\). Under the paraxial ray approximation, what is the focal length of the mirror according to the Cartesian sign convention?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of curvature of the concave mirror: \(R = 30\text{ cm}\). Light is incident from the front of the reflecting surface.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
According to the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured opposite to the direction of incident light are negative. For a concave mirror, the centre of curvature lies in front of the mirror, so \(R = -30\text{ cm}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For spherical mirrors under paraxial ray approximation, the focal length \(f\) is related to the radius of curvature \(R\) by: \[f = \frac{R}{2}\] Suppliers of optical surfaces define focal length consistently under this convention.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(R = -30\text{ cm}\): \[f = \frac{-30\text{ cm}}{2} = -15\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
A concave mirror has a real principal focus located in front of its reflecting surface, giving a negative focal length of \(-15\text{ cm}\).

Final Answer:
The focal length of the concave mirror is \(-15\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Critical angle for glass air boundary

questiontext.text: The refractive index of a dense flint glass with respect to air is \(1.50\). What is the sine of the critical angle for total internal reflection at the glass-air boundary?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Refractive index of the denser medium (glass): \(n_1 = 1.50 = \frac{3}{2}\). Refractive index of the rarer medium (air): \(n_2 = 1.00\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Light travels from the optically denser medium (glass) towards the rarer medium (air).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The critical angle \(i_c\) is given by Snell's law when the angle of refraction is \(90^\circ\): \[\sin(i_c) = \frac{n_2}{n_1} = \frac{1}{n}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(n = \frac{3}{2}\): \[\sin(i_c) = \frac{1}{3/2} = \frac{2}{3}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(n_1 > n_2\), the critical angle exists and its sine is strictly less than \(1\), namely \(\frac{2}{3}\).

Final Answer:
The sine of the critical angle is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Refractive index from speed of light

questiontext.text: Light propagates in a transparent dielectric medium with a speed of \(2.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Taking the speed of light in vacuum as \(c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\), what is the absolute refractive index of the medium?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light in the medium: \(v = 2.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Speed of light in vacuum: \(c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The medium is homogeneous, isotropic, and non-magnetic.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The absolute refractive index \(n\) of a medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium: \[n = \frac{c}{v}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the definition: \[n = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}}{2.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}} = 1.50\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The refractive index is dimensionless and greater than 1 for any material medium, yielding \(1.50\).

Final Answer:
The absolute refractive index of the medium is \(1.50\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Optical power of a convex lens

questiontext.text: A thin converging lens has a focal length of \(+25\text{ cm}\). What is the optical power of this lens?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Focal length of the convex lens: \(f = +25\text{ cm} = +0.25\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The lens is thin and placed in air. Focal length in metres carries a positive sign for a converging lens.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The optical power \(P\) of a lens in dioptres (\(\text{D} = \text{m}^{-1}\)) is the reciprocal of its focal length expressed in metres: \[P = \frac{1}{f\text{ (in metres)}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(f = +0.25\text{ m}\): \[P = \frac{1}{0.25\text{ m}} = +4.0\text{ D}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
A positive focal length yields a positive dioptre value, confirming a converging lens of power \(+4.0\text{ D}\).

Final Answer:
The optical power of the lens is \(+4.0\text{ D}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Equivalent focal length of lenses in contact

questiontext.text: Two thin lenses of powers \(+3.5\text{ D}\) and \(-1.5\text{ D}\) are placed in coaxial contact. What is the equivalent focal length of this combination?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Power of the first lens: \(P_1 = +3.5\text{ D}\). Power of the second lens: \(P_2 = -1.5\text{ D}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The lenses are thin and held in intimate contact along a common principal axis.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total power of thin lenses in contact is algebraic: \[P = P_1 + P_2\] The equivalent focal length \(F\) is: \[F = \frac{1}{P}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate total power: \[P = +3.5\text{ D} + (-1.5\text{ D}) = +2.0\text{ D}\] Now calculate equivalent focal length: \[F = \frac{1}{+2.0\text{ D}} = +0.50\text{ m} = +50\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The net power is positive, so the combination behaves as a converging lens with focal length \(+50\text{ cm}\).

Final Answer:
The equivalent focal length of the combination is \(+50\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Magnifying power of astronomical telescope at infinity

questiontext.text: An astronomical refracting telescope has an objective of focal length \(140\text{ cm}\) and an eyepiece of focal length \(5.0\text{ cm}\). What is the magnifying power of the telescope in normal adjustment (final image at infinity)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Focal length of objective: \(f_o = 140\text{ cm}\). Focal length of eyepiece: \(f_e = 5.0\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Normal adjustment implies that both the object and the final image are at infinity.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of angular magnification (magnifying power) of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is: \[m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the focal lengths: \[m = \frac{140\text{ cm}}{5.0\text{ cm}} = 28\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The magnifying power is dimensionless and exceeds unity as expected for a telescope, giving \(28\).

Final Answer:
The magnifying power of the telescope in normal adjustment is \(28\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Virtual image height formed by concave mirror

questiontext.text: An object of height \(4.5\text{ cm}\) is placed at a distance of \(12\text{ cm}\) in front of a concave spherical mirror of focal length \(15\text{ cm}\). What is the height of the virtual image formed by the mirror?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Object height: \(h = 4.5\text{ cm}\). Object distance: \(u = -12\text{ cm}\). Focal length of concave mirror: \(f = -15\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All distances are measured from the mirror pole. Distances opposite to incident light are negative; heights above the principal axis are positive.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The mirror formula and linear magnification relation are: \[\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}, \quad m = \frac{h'}{h} = -\frac{v}{u}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Solve for image position \(v\): \[\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{-15} - \frac{1}{-12} = -\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{-4 + 5}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\text{ cm}^{-1}\] Therefore, \(v = +60\text{ cm}\). Now compute magnification: \[m = -\frac{v}{u} = -\frac{+60}{-12} = +5\] The image height is: \[h' = m \times h = 5 \times 4.5\text{ cm} = 22.5\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Because the object is between the pole and focus (\(|u| < |f|\)), the image is virtual, erect, magnified, and located behind the mirror with height \(22.5\text{ cm}\).

Final Answer:
The height of the virtual image is \(22.5\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Image location in convex spherical mirror

questiontext.text: An object is placed at a distance of \(30\text{ cm}\) in front of a convex spherical mirror of focal length \(20\text{ cm}\). What is the distance of the image from the pole of the mirror?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Object distance: \(u = -30\text{ cm}\). Focal length of convex mirror: \(f = +20\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Light travels from left to right. Distances measured behind the mirror (in the direction of incident light) are positive.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Apply the spherical mirror equation: \[\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} \implies \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{u}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{+20} - \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{3 + 2}{60} = \frac{5}{60} = \frac{1}{12}\text{ cm}^{-1}\] Thus: \[v = +12\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The positive sign indicates a virtual image formed \(12\text{ cm}\) behind the reflecting surface, consistent with the diverging nature of convex mirrors.

Final Answer:
The image is formed \(12\text{ cm}\) behind the mirror.

answer.text: \(12\text{ cm}\text{ in front of the mirror}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Apparent shift of submerged object in water

questiontext.text: A tank is filled with water of refractive index \(\frac{4}{3}\) to a depth of \(12.0\text{ cm}\). A small coin rests at the bottom of the tank. When viewed normally from above, by what distance does the coin appear to be raised?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Real depth of the water layer: \(d = 12.0\text{ cm}\). Refractive index of water: \(n = \frac{4}{3}\). Viewing angle is near-normal.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Paraxial approximation applies for near-normal viewing. Shift is directed upwards towards the observer.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The apparent depth \(d'\) and the apparent upward shift \(\Delta y\) are given by: \[d' = \frac{d}{n}, \quad \Delta y = d - d' = d\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate apparent depth: \[d' = \frac{12.0}{4/3} = 12.0 \times \frac{3}{4} = 9.0\text{ cm}\] Then the apparent upward displacement is: \[\Delta y = 12.0\text{ cm} - 9.0\text{ cm} = 3.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The bottom appears closer to the surface by \(3.0\text{ cm}\), leaving an apparent depth of \(9.0\text{ cm}\).

Final Answer:
The coin appears to be raised by \(3.0\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Apparent depth of two immiscible liquids

questiontext.text: A cylindrical beaker contains a layer of water (refractive index \(\frac{4}{3}\)) of depth \(8.0\text{ cm}\), above which floats an immiscible oil layer (refractive index \(1.40\)) of depth \(7.0\text{ cm}\). When viewed normally from air, what is the total apparent depth of the bottom of the beaker?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
First layer (water): \(d_1 = 8.0\text{ cm}\), \(n_1 = \frac{4}{3}\). Second layer (oil): \(d_2 = 7.0\text{ cm}\), \(n_2 = 1.40 = \frac{7}{5}\). Viewing medium is air (\(n = 1.0\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Viewing is along the normal to the horizontal interfaces. Paraxial approximation holds.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For multiple horizontal layers viewed normally, the total apparent depth \(d_{\text{app}}\) is the sum of the apparent depths of individual layers: \[d_{\text{app}} = \sum \frac{d_i}{n_i} = \frac{d_1}{n_1} + \frac{d_2}{n_2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the apparent depth contributed by the water layer: \[d_1' = \frac{8.0}{4/3} = 8.0 \times \frac{3}{4} = 6.0\text{ cm}\] Calculate the apparent depth contributed by the oil layer: \[d_2' = \frac{7.0}{1.40} = 5.0\text{ cm}\] Total apparent depth is: \[d_{\text{app}} = 6.0\text{ cm} + 5.0\text{ cm} = 11.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total physical depth is \(8.0 + 7.0 = 15.0\text{ cm}\). Since both media are denser than air, the apparent depth must be smaller, yielding \(11.0\text{ cm}\).

Final Answer:
The total apparent depth is \(11.0\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Lateral shift through parallel glass slab

questiontext.text: A ray of light is incident at an angle of \(60^\circ\) on a glass slab of thickness \(3.0\text{ cm}\) and refractive index \(\sqrt{3}\). What is the lateral displacement suffered by the ray upon emerging from the slab?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Angle of incidence: \(i = 60^\circ\). Thickness of glass slab: \(t = 3.0\text{ cm}\). Refractive index of slab: \(n = \sqrt{3}\). Surrounding medium is air (\(n = 1\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Opposite faces of the slab are plane and parallel. The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Snell's law: \[\sin r = \frac{\sin i}{n}\] Lateral displacement \(x\): \[x = \frac{t \sin(i - r)}{\cos r}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Find angle of refraction \(r\): \[\sin r = \frac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}/2}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{2} \implies r = 30^\circ\] Now evaluate the lateral shift formula with \(i - r = 60^\circ - 30^\circ = 30^\circ\): \[x = \frac{3.0 \sin 30^\circ}{\cos 30^\circ} = 3.0 \tan 30^\circ = 3.0 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}\text{ cm} \approx 1.732\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The lateral displacement \(\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\) is strictly less than the slab thickness \(3.0\text{ cm}\), in accordance with geometric optics.

Final Answer:
The lateral displacement of the ray is \(\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Illuminated circle radius from submerged source

questiontext.text: A point source of light is placed at the bottom of a water reservoir of depth \(\sqrt{7}\text{ m}\). The refractive index of water is \(\frac{4}{3}\). What is the radius of the circular patch on the water surface through which light emerges into air?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Depth of water: \(d = \sqrt{7}\text{ m}\). Refractive index of water: \(n = \frac{4}{3}\). Refractive index of air: \(1.0\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Light rays incident at the water-air interface at angles greater than the critical angle \(i_c\) undergo total internal reflection and cannot emerge.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Critical angle relation: \[\sin(i_c) = \frac{1}{n} = \frac{3}{4}\] Geometric radius of the illuminated circle: \[R = d \tan(i_c) = \frac{d \sin(i_c)}{\cos(i_c)} = \frac{d}{\sqrt{n^2 - 1}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \(\tan(i_c)\): \[\cos(i_c) = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2(i_c)} = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{9}{16}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}\] Thus: \[\tan(i_c) = \frac{3/4}{\sqrt{7}/4} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{7}}\] Now find radius \(R\): \[R = d \tan(i_c) = \sqrt{7}\text{ m} \times \frac{3}{\sqrt{7}} = 3.0\text{ m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The radius \(3.0\text{ m}\) gives a well-defined circular aperture of diameter \(6.0\text{ m}\) beyond which all light is totally reflected internally.

Final Answer:
The radius of the circular patch on the water surface is \(3.0\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Minimum deviation angle for equilateral prism

questiontext.text: A triangular glass prism has a refracting angle of \(A = 60^\circ\) and a refractive index of \(\sqrt{2}\). What is the angle of minimum deviation produced by this prism?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Prism refracting angle: \(A = 60^\circ\). Refractive index of prism material: \(n = \sqrt{2}\). Surrounding medium is air.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
At the minimum deviation angle \(D_m\), the light ray passes symmetrically through the prism, so \(r_1 = r_2 = \frac{A}{2}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The prism formula relates refractive index \(n\) to prism angle \(A\) and minimum deviation \(D_m\): \[n = \frac{\sin\left(\frac{A + D_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(A = 60^\circ\) and \(n = \sqrt{2}\): \[\sin(A/2) = \sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\] \[\sqrt{2} = \frac{\sin\left(\frac{60^\circ + D_m}{2}\right)}{1/2} \implies \sin\left(\frac{60^\circ + D_m}{2}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\] Since \(\sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\): \[\frac{60^\circ + D_m}{2} = 45^\circ \implies 60^\circ + D_m = 90^\circ \implies D_m = 30^\circ\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The angle of incidence at minimum deviation is \(i = 45^\circ\) and refraction angle is \(r = 30^\circ\), satisfying Snell's law \(\sin 45^\circ / \sin 30^\circ = (1/\sqrt{2})/(1/2) = \sqrt{2}\). Thus \(D_m = 30^\circ\).

Final Answer:
The angle of minimum deviation is \(30^\circ\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Deviation produced by small angle thin prism

questiontext.text: A thin glass prism of refracting angle \(4.0^\circ\) is made of glass of refractive index \(1.54\). What is the angle of deviation suffered by a ray of light passing through this thin prism at small incidence?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Prism angle: \(A = 4.0^\circ\). Refractive index of prism material: \(n = 1.54\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The prism is thin (\(A < 10^\circ\)) and the angle of incidence is small, allowing small-angle approximations \(\sin \theta \approx \theta\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a thin prism, the deviation \(\delta\) is independent of the incidence angle to first order: \[\delta = (n - 1)A\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values: \[\delta = (1.54 - 1) \times 4.0^\circ = 0.54 \times 4.0^\circ = 2.16^\circ\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The deviation \(2.16^\circ\) is small and directly proportional to the refracting angle \(A\).

Final Answer:
The angle of deviation is \(2.16^\circ\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Refraction at single spherical convex surface

questiontext.text: A point object in air (refractive index \(1.0\)) is placed at a distance of \(40\text{ cm}\) from the vertex of a convex spherical glass surface of radius of curvature \(+15\text{ cm}\). If the refractive index of glass is \(1.50\), at what distance from the vertex inside the glass is the image formed?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Refractive index of initial medium (air): \(n_1 = 1.0\). Refractive index of second medium (glass): \(n_2 = 1.50\). Object distance: \(u = -40\text{ cm}\). Radius of curvature: \(R = +15\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Distances are measured from the pole/vertex of the spherical surface. Light travels from left to right; the convex surface has its centre of curvature in the glass (positive \(R\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The formula for refraction at a single spherical surface is: \[\frac{n_2}{v} - \frac{n_1}{u} = \frac{n_2 - n_1}{R}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given parameters: \[\frac{1.5}{v} - \frac{1.0}{-40} = \frac{1.5 - 1.0}{+15}\] \[\frac{1.5}{v} + \frac{1}{40} = \frac{0.5}{15} = \frac{1}{30}\] Rearrange to solve for \(\frac{1.5}{v}\): \[\frac{1.5}{v} = \frac{1}{30} - \frac{1}{40} = \frac{4 - 3}{120} = \frac{1}{120}\text{ cm}^{-1}\] Therefore: \[v = 1.5 \times 120 = +180\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The positive sign demonstrates that a real converging image is formed \(180\text{ cm}\) inside the glass medium.

Final Answer:
The image is formed at \(+180\text{ cm}\) from the vertex inside the glass.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Radius of curvature for equiconvex glass lens

questiontext.text: An equiconvex thin lens made of glass with refractive index \(1.50\) has a focal length of \(20\text{ cm}\) in air. What is the magnitude of the radius of curvature of each of its spherical surfaces?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Focal length of lens: \(f = +20\text{ cm}\). Refractive index of lens material: \(n = 1.50\). Surrounding medium is air (\(n_{\text{med}} = 1\)). The lens is equiconvex.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
For an equiconvex lens, the first surface is convex to incident light (\(R_1 = +R\)) and the second is concave (\(R_2 = -R\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Apply the Lens Maker's Formula: \[\frac{1}{f} = (n - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(R_1 = +R\) and \(R_2 = -R\): \[\frac{1}{f} = (1.50 - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R} - \left(-\frac{1}{R}\right)\right) = 0.50 \times \frac{2}{R} = \frac{1}{R}\] Equating to \(\frac{1}{f}\): \[\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{20\text{ cm}} \implies R = 20\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
For glass of \(n = 1.5\), the focal length of an equiconvex lens is exactly equal to its radius of curvature, verifying \(R = 20\text{ cm}\).

Final Answer:
The radius of curvature of each surface is \(20\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_RAYOPTICS_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Focal length change of lens immersed in water

questiontext.text: A biconvex glass lens (refractive index \(n_g = 1.50\)) has a focal length of \(20\text{ cm}\) in air. What is its new focal length when it is completely immersed in water of refractive index \(n_w = \frac{4}{3}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Focal length in air: \(f_{\text{air}} = 20\text{ cm}\). Refractive index of glass: \(n_g = 1.50 = \frac{3}{2}\). Refractive index of water: \(n_w = \frac{4}{3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The radii of curvature \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) remain identical in both media.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The focal length in a surrounding medium is: \[\frac{1}{f_{\text{med}}} = \left(\frac{n_g}{n_{\text{med}}} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)\] The ratio of focal lengths is: \[\frac{f_{\text{water}}}{f_{\text{air}}} = \frac{n_g - 1}{\frac{n_g}{n_w} - 1}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
